horizon_scenarios.scenario: isotropic radiance L, horizon raised (terrain obstruction) by h: E = pi L cos^2(h) against E(0) = pi L; a horizon depressed below the true horizon (open site) leaves E = pi L because directions below 0 deg elevation never illuminate the upward board (Omega+)
horizon_scenarios.note: flat-horizon geometric factor only; the real site horizon and white-board angular response are unmeasured, so this bounds geometry, not response

notes: timing offsets use the signed central-difference band rate (per minute); a positive offset means later in time, and the scenario values carry the rate's sign rather than a magnitudenight-floor ratios involve common device gain that may cancel; background colour structure and time variation do not cancel
no background subtraction is applied anywhere in this packet
